migrated_scope: Internal offline extraction consumes owned VerifiedBundleSource handles rather than reopenable filesystem paths. Exact ordinal AssetPath lookup rejects duplicate matches within/across containers, including repeated pointers to one object. Only class49 TextAsset resolves; its name must be the filename or final-extension-free stem. Script bytes, including NUL and invalid UTF-8, are copied without text conversion; the requested script must be nonempty.

Supported format subset: UnityFS 6/7/8 with compression 0/2/3 (none/raw LZ4/LZ4HC), front/end block info, canonical LZ4 termination and reviewed 0x200 padding semantics. SerializedFile22 requires little endian, Windows64 target19, engine2021.3.45f2 and embedded class142/class49 trees matching the reviewed 58-node/9-node parsing semantics. Inert node versions/non-alignment metadata bits are normalized; unknown layouts reject.

File identities combine verified bundle name and exact directory entry within one data/package/version context. CAB basenames never alias. External PPtrs require explicit source-file/exact-external-path/target-file bindings; no basename fallback, automatic dependencies, filesystem probing, HTTP or external open.

Bounded inputs: 1–24 distinct bundles, 64 MiB each and 128 MiB aggregate; expansion 64 MiB per bundle/128 MiB aggregate. Further limits cover block info/blocks, serialized files, metadata/types/trees, objects, container entries and encoded path bytes before decoding, dependencies/externals and 16-MiB script payloads. These are allocation/expansion ceilings, not a peak-RSS guarantee. Streams are scoped, results own detached bytes and cancellation is checked through chunk/block/LZ4/metadata/object/container work.

91 focused tests passed against original UnityPy 1.25.4 writer-generated SerializedFile/UnityFS fixtures and independent lz4 4.4.5 compression. Test-only AssetsTools.NET [3.0.5] independently reads retained hash-verified writer files and m_Script as bytes; malformed inputs never enter that package decoder. Fixtures contain authored payloads/trees, not game payloads or class databases. Runtime Core has no decoder package dependency; only the common-string table is vendored under its accompanying MIT notice.
